clue.text: A heartless story, song and dance expert

indicators.note: a heartless word loses its central letter, here the middle of the seven-letter story word

parts.note: a story is a piece of fiction
a song and dance is a fuss, which is ado

explanation.surface: A cold, unfeeling tale offered alongside some musical theatre and an expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes T, the middle letter, from FICTION, leaving FICION.
explanation.definitionFit: An aficionado is a devotee with deep knowledge of a pastime, so a connoisseur or expert.

clue.text: Trace bird from down under over time

indicators.note: over here means spanning or covering, so the bird's letters go around the time letter
in a down clue, reading from the bottom up turns the letters backwards; it also hints at the bird's New Zealand home

parts.note: the moa is an extinct flightless bird of New Zealand

explanation.surface: Finding a faint sign of an Antipodean bird from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from down under' reads MOA upwards as AOM (and hints at New Zealand); 'over' puts it around T.
explanation.definitionFit: A trace is a tiny amount, and an atom is likewise a minute quantity, as in 'not an atom of truth'.

clue.text: Being still inebriated after partying and missing bed

indicators.note: after a party the letters of the drunken word are in disarray, so they are rearranged
missing tells us the letters of the sleeping word are taken out of the pool first

explanation.surface: Someone motionless because they were drunk after a party and never made it to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Take B, E and D from INEBRIATED, leaving INRIATE, and 'after partying' shuffles those seven letters into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is a state of rest or lack of motion, the condition of being still.

clue.text: Put behind bars at Los Angeles, premier written up worldwide

parts.note: to intern is to confine or imprison

indicators.note: in a down clue, written up means the letters are set down from bottom to top, so read backwards

parts.note: the premier is number one, written No 1 with the figure read as I

explanation.surface: A political leader is jailed in Los Angeles, and the story is reported around the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written up' turns LA + NO + I (No 1, the premier) round to give IONAL.
explanation.definitionFit: International means across or between nations, so spanning the world: a near synonym for worldwide.

clue.text: Conversion of Saint Paul, short of a romantic ceremony

indicators.note: conversion means changing form, so the letters of the saint's name are reshaped; it also nods to Paul's famous conversion
short of here means lacking, so the letter a is removed from the pool

explanation.surface: The Conversion of Saint Paul, minus something, is likened to a romantic ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop one A from SAINTPAUL and 'Conversion of' rearranges the remaining eight letters; the plural answer names a single event.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuptials is a formal word for a wedding, the ceremony at which a couple marry.

clue.text: Beginning golf, tee off and clean up

indicators.note: off means taken away, so the letter named by tee is dropped

parts.note: a debut is a first appearance, a beginning
tee is the spelt-out name of the letter T
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A golfer making a start on the course, teeing off, then tidying up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tee' is the letter T spelt out, and 'off' removes it from DEBUTG.
explanation.definitionFit: To debug is to remove errors from software, cleaning it up so it works.

clue.text: Python meat?

parts.note: the tinned meat made famous by the Monty Python comedy team's sketch, rather than a snake's dinner

explanation.surface: What a large snake eats.
explanation.walkthrough: The snake is a red herring: Monty Python, the British comedy troupe, sang endlessly about this canned meat in a café sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is a brand of tinned pork luncheon meat, the star of a famous Monty Python sketch.

clue.text: Arrested by cop, charged journalist had a swagger

indicators.note: something arrested by a policeman is held inside him, so the cop's letters surround it

parts.note: PC is a police constable
to charge is to rush forward, so ran
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter, charged and held by police, strutted around regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' is not about a criminal charge: it means rushed, RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To prance is to move with exaggerated, showy steps, which is strutting with a swagger.

clue.text: Absorbed in Batman, get out snack food

indicators.note: absorbed in means held inside, so the answer sits within the run of clue words

explanation.surface: Engrossed in a Batman comic, someone is told to fetch a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from batMAN through GET OUT to the S of Snack; 'snack' is not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangetouts are flat pea pods eaten whole, a vegetable and so a kind of food.

clue.text: Ring writer — dope's overturned sports car?

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O
a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, so in an across clue the word is read backwards

parts.note: dope is cannabis, also called pot; 's is a link (dope is)

explanation.surface: Calling a writer to say a fool's sports car has flipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition by example: an open-top is one kind of sports car.
explanation.definitionFit: Many sports cars are convertibles with no roof, described as open-top.

clue.text: Pshaw! Bad weather in country

parts.note: pshaw and bah are both exclamations of contempt
rain is the classic example of bad weather

explanation.surface: A grumble about foul weather in some country.
explanation.definitionFit: Bahrain is an island kingdom in the Persian Gulf, an independent nation.

clue.text: Fussy bar being disconnected from net?

definitions.meaning: Barnet is Cockney rhyming slang for hair (from Barnet Fair), so splitting BAR from NET is splitting the hair

explanation.surface: A finicky bar where the internet connection keeps dropping.
explanation.walkthrough: BARNET, short for 'Barnet Fair', is Cockney rhyming slang for hair; separating its BAR from its NET literally splits it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair-splitting is making overly fine distinctions, which is fussy, pedantic behaviour.

clue.text: Clio goes around in one

parts.note: the Renault Clio is a small car, and the space a car needs to turn round is measured as a circle

explanation.surface: Clio, the Muse of History, travelling around in something.
explanation.walkthrough: Clio suggests the Greek Muse, but it is the Renault Clio hatchback, which does a U-turn within this circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's turning circle is the smallest circular space in which it can make a complete turn.

clue.text: Expert more or less puts up with losing northern operations

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
c, short for circa, means approximately

indicators.note: losing means a letter is lost from the word before it

parts.note: to endure something is to put up with it

explanation.surface: A professional reluctantly tolerates the closing of the northern branch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes N from ENDURES, leaving EDURES.
explanation.definitionFit: Procedures are established ways of doing things, a series of operations or actions.

clue.text: Hard to put down in print in proper English

indicators.note: in puts the print letters inside the word for proper

parts.note: real and proper both mean genuine
a dab is a fingerprint

explanation.surface: Something difficult to set down in print in correct English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard' looks like the abbreviation H, but 'Hard to put down' is the definition. DAB is slang for a fingerprint.
explanation.definitionFit: A readable book is enjoyable and engaging, the sort a reader finds difficult to stop reading.

clue.text: Would take essence of arrowroot desultorily in retirement

indicators.note: in retirement says the hidden letters are read backwards
the essence is the inner core, so letters are drawn from inside the words

explanation.surface: Someone habitually consumed arrowroot extract in a half-hearted way in their old age.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft made 'take essence' part of the definition, but 'take essence of' signals the hidden letters; 'Would' alone is the definition. 'in retirement' reverses OTDESU.
explanation.definitionFit: Would can express past habit, as in 'he would walk daily', meaning the same as 'he used to'.

clue.text: Female pandas possibly canoodling

definitions.meaning: panda cars are British police cars; a female version of cars, like host to hostess
the noun canoodling means kisses and cuddles

explanation.surface: Female giant pandas getting affectionate with one another.
explanation.walkthrough: Panda cars were British police patrol cars. Adding the feminine ending -ess to car makes CARESS, so female cars would be this word.
explanation.definitionFit: Caresses are gentle loving strokes and touches, which is what canoodling consists of.

clue.text: Clan member not taking sides — Scot just wins

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its ends, so each of the next three words loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A neutral Highlander pleased with victory alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not taking sides' looks like neutrality but strips the end letters of Scot, just and wins.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin is a relative, and a clan is an extended family group, so a cousin is one of the clan.

clue.text: Heathen's computer work at risk?

definitions.meaning: Heathen's is short for heathen is; a heathen is not saved in the religious sense
work on a computer that has not yet been stored is ... and could be lost

explanation.surface: A pagan's computer files are in danger of being lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsaved means not redeemed spiritually, and also describes a file not yet stored on disk.

clue.text: China's put out over this computer graduate's smuggled in

indicators.note: smuggled in means slipped inside, so the graduate goes within the computer

parts.note: a tablet is a small handheld computer
MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: China releases a computer with something sneaked inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is not the country but crockery, laid down on top of this; 's here means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A table mat sits under plates and dishes, so tableware is placed on top of it.

clue.text: Three daughters — two blocking stubborn ass, third daughter at sea

indicators.note: blocking means sitting in the way, so the two letters are placed inside the animal

parts.note: the mule is proverbially stubborn and is part ass
two of the three daughters, each D, the abbreviation for daughter
the third daughter is one more D

explanation.surface: Three daughters stuck on an obstinate donkey, with the last one floundering.
explanation.walkthrough: D is the abbreviation for daughter; two Ds go inside MULE, and the third follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at sea is to be confused and bewildered, which is being muddled.

clue.text: Objective is not accruing money at bank?

definitions.meaning: objective means impartial, with no personal stake

definitions.text: is not accruing money at bank?
definitions.meaning: an account earning no interest could jokingly be called ...; the phrase stands for an adjective

explanation.surface: A neutral observer notes that savings are earning nothing at the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as DIS + INTERESTED: not earning interest on a deposit.
explanation.definitionFit: Disinterested means impartial and unbiased, free of personal advantage, which is being objective.

clue.text: New page in Lear screenplay perhaps

definitions.text: New page in Lear screenplay perhaps

parts.words: New page in Lear screenplay perhaps
parts.note: a newly added page is an additional one, and a page boy in a filmed King Lear would be a minor non-speaking role

explanation.surface: A fresh page inserted into a film script of King Lear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'page' plays on two senses: a sheet added to the script, and a servant boy played by a bit-part actor in the film.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is both something additional and a film actor in a small background role.

clue.text: Men's game

definitions.meaning: ... describes an all-male event, as in a ... night
a male deer, hunted as game

explanation.walkthrough: A stag night or stag do is the British name for a bachelor party.
explanation.definitionFit: Stag means for men only, and a stag is a deer, an animal hunted as game.

clue.text: Channel Four's in guide shown by TV, but not Five

indicators.note: in puts the numeral inside the guide word

parts.note: a rule is a guide to conduct
IV is four in Roman numerals; 's means is

indicators.note: but not says the following letter is taken away from what precedes it

parts.note: V is five in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Channel Four features in a TV listings guide, though Channel Five is left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Channel Four and Five are British TV channels, but here the numbers are Roman numerals; 'but not' takes V from TV, leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: A rivulet is a very small stream, a narrow channel of flowing water.

clue.text: In Paris, and after training, one's invaluable in the kitchen

indicators.note: after places the French word behind the word for training

parts.note: skill is ability acquired through training
et is French for and

explanation.surface: A cookery student in Paris, once trained, becomes indispensable in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A skillet is a frying pan, a basic piece of cookware that any kitchen relies on.

clue.text: Eleven maybe were moaning out loud

indicators.note: out loud means the word is spoken, so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: sighed means let out a moan or groan

explanation.surface: Perhaps eleven people were complaining audibly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eleven' is a football or cricket team; 'were' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a sports team, and teams in football and cricket have eleven players.

clue.text: One's associated with a thinly-stretched body that's short of member

definitions.text: One's associated with a thinly-stretched body that's short of member

parts.words: One's associated with a thinly-stretched body that's short of member
parts.note: a creature with a long thin body and short legs, the limbs being members

explanation.surface: Someone linked to a lanky organisation that has too few members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' means a limb, not someone in a club: the dog has very short legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Sausage dog is a nickname for the dachshund, a dog with a long body and very short legs.
